note: The bands the Quickie 500 plant has to land in, from docs/QUICKIE-STAGE1.md, which derives each from Glen Spickler's Quickie 500 (American Aircraft Modeler, December 1972, and its plan, Outerzone oz6868, measured), RCM's product test of his kit, Old School Model Works' throws for its kit of the design, Peter Chinn's bench test of the K&B 40 R/C and APC's propeller data (scripts/quickie-derive.js prints the derived figures). Set from the derivation before the plant was flown. Never widened to pass; argue in the derivation instead.

q1_top.source: level speed at full throttle, derived 39.37 m/s (88 mph) from the open K&B on the APC 9 x 6 against the built up drag; the band 10 percent either side of it (35.4 to 43.3) held inside 15 percent of Spickler's 'the models will fly around 100 mph on the straightaway' (38.0 to 51.4), so it is both the derivation's and the class's

q2_stall.source: sqrt(2W / rho S CLmax), derived 9.31; alphaStall is CLmax / CLalpha, 0.90 / 4.866; the band the Stik's in proportion, 6 percent under and 14 over

q3_glide.source: L/D at 1.4 Vs, 13.04 m/s, derived 8.99 (its best 9.48 at 11.1 m/s); 11 percent either side, the Stik's. FM, March 1979: 'the glide ratio will amaze you ... The glide is very long and flat'

q4_climb.source: the best climb at a held airspeed, full throttle, derived 18.70 m/s at 21.6; 30 percent under and 20 over, the Stik's. FM: 'with a honking .40 up front it will do anything vertical'

q5_roll.source: full aileron at OSMW's 1/2 in on the 1 in strip aileron (30 deg, 20.7 through the Edge's knee) from level flat out, as the helix angle: Clda over -Clp times the throw, derived 0.1159 (404 deg/s at 39.4 m/s); 20 percent either side, the Stik's

q5_stop.source: fast but not twitchy: 0.3 s of full aileron from level flat out, then the stick centred: the roll mode's time constant is 9 ms at 39.4 m/s (Ixx over the roll damping), so at 404 deg/s the bank runs on 3.6 deg after the stick is centred; the band twice that, 7 deg, and the rate under 20 deg/s 0.3 s after, when the wing's damping has stopped it

q6_pylon.source: a level 180 deg pylon turn at 6 g from flat out at full throttle, ailerons and elevator only: the point mass the plant's polar makes loses 4.79 percent of its speed (39.37 to 37.49 m/s) on a 24.2 m radius in 2.07 s, the lift that pulls 6 g costing 36 times the level flight's induced drag; the loss 35 percent either side, the radius 15 percent; and flat without rudder, the sideslip under 5 deg (Spickler: 'Properly trimmed, the Quicky 500 will fly through the turns flat without the need of any rudder control')

q7_coast.source: carrying its speed: from level flat out the throttle to idle, the height held, derived 9.83 s and 225.8 m before it is down to 1.5 Vs, 13.97 m/s; 15 percent either side

q8_hard_turn.source: no snap in the corners (Spickler: 'no tendency to snap roll in the corners'): a level 180 deg turn at 10 g from flat out, derived alpha 5.9 deg against the stall's 10.6, 10.25 percent of the speed lost on a 12.8 m radius; the loss 35 percent either side, and after the roll in the bank held within 12 deg of the turn's and no roll rate past 90 deg/s, a snap's signature

q9_neutral.source: from level flat out rolled to 20 deg, every stick let go: the lateral model's spiral root is -0.028, a half life of 25 s, so it holds its bank, 18.2 deg after 3 s; Spickler: 'It points well on the straightaway'

q11_prop_torque.source: static full throttle, rolling left: the open K&B's 0.3528 N m at the 9 x 6's 14,831 rpm, 15 percent either side

q12_rest.source: the drawn model at rest: the plan's 2 1/4 in wheels and the skid's tip on the grass, 6.50 deg nose up with the CG 0.1325 m up and 14.6 percent on the skid; 1 deg, 5 mm

q13_takeoff.source: ROG, as the class takes off, full throttle from standing on grass held three point at the rest attitude: derived 5.66 m at 11.90 m/s, the wheels at 0.08 and the skid's 14.6 percent at 0.35; the distance 30 percent either side, the speed between 1.1 and 1.5 Vs. Its first form lifted the tail at 8 m/s and rotated at 1.2 Vs, 6.12 m at 12.39 m/s; flown, the wheels' drag under the CG and the thrust line over it held the nose down on the mains until 32 m/s, so the technique changed to three point, as RCM describes it: 'extremely easy tail dragger take-offs' (docs/QUICKIE-STAGE1.md)

q14_landing.source: a glide at idle, a flare, on the mains and the skid: at rest within 1.5 deg of Q12, no hull or prop, and no bounce past 5 cm (FM: 'Once it's down there is little or no bouncing tendency')

q15_idle.source: the engine at Chinn's 2,700 rpm idle keeps turning and its 0.81 N is under the 1.86 N the grass holds the aircraft with: it stands

q16_unmoved.source: the five inch's canonical replay hash and every other aircraft's recorded flight hash in Node, from main's module at 1fd93f3, before the Quickie existed

q17_cross_host.source: the Quickie's recorded take off, roll, pylon turn and inverted run, state trace hash, Node against headless Chrome

q18_inverted.source: RCM's '15% Symmetrical' at no incidence: on its back flat out it flies within 5 percent of its upright speed, the Stik's band, and holds level with a push, derived 1.47 deg of down elevator, 0.094 of the stick; 40 percent either side. FM: 'Inverted flight is almost as easy as upright with only a hint of down trim needed'
